Medical History

- Current health concerns and risk factors:
  - Severe headache for 3 days, sudden onset; described as “blinding,” mostly diffuse but worse over the right eye.
  - Photophobia (sensitivity to strong light) and intermittent visual disturbances described as “shooting light”/flashing.
  - Partial response to ibuprofen; pain severity reported up to 8/10, reducing to ~5/10 at times.
  - Associated mild nausea but no vomiting.
  - Intermittent stabbing pain when standing up quickly or moving the head.
  - No fever, no sinus symptoms, no nasal bleeding, no smell/taste change, no focal neurological symptoms (no numbness/tingling/weakness).
  - Impacting function: difficulty focusing at work; missed workdays.

- Relevant family medical history:
  - Mother has severe migraines, including vomiting.
  - No other family history recorded.

- Medications (including OTC or shared medications):
  - Combined oral contraceptive pill — started ~1 year ago (specific pill/name not documented).
  - Ibuprofen PRN for headaches (OTC) — dose/route/frequency not documented.
  - Paracetamol was recommended as an additional analgesic (patient advised can take with the prescribed medication) — no prescription recorded.
  - Clinician offered to prescribe a stronger analgesic “similar to ibuprofen” — prescription name/dose/frequency not documented.
  - No known drug allergies.

- Immunisation status reviewed:
  - Not recorded.

- Sexual and reproductive health:
  - Currently using combined oral contraceptive pill for ~1 year.
  - Blood pressure was checked at pharmacy when pill was started ~1 year ago and reported as normal then.
  - Clinician noted combined OCP may need review if migraines with aura are confirmed; advised BP check at forthcoming exam.
  - Pregnancy/contraceptive complications/STI history not recorded.

- Physical activity and nutrition:
  - Not recorded (patient reported possible lack of energy attributed to headache).

- Alcohol, tobacco, and substance use:
  - Tobacco: denies smoking.
  - Alcohol: reports drinking “probably like, three, once a week” (patient’s wording).
  - Other recreational drugs: denies use.
  - Use of ibuprofen intermittently for headache as above.

- Hearing loss or concerns:
  - Not recorded.

- Mood/mental health (including depression, self-harm risk):
  - Not recorded.

- Vision problems or recent changes:
  - Reports photophobia and intermittent flashing/shooting lights.
  - Recent eye check reported with “nothing changed” in vision.

- Family and social relationships, caring responsibilities:

  - No caring responsibilities recorded.

Management Plan

- Key management actions and recommendations provided:
  - Arrange and attend a clinical appointment for full neurological examination including fundoscopy and BP measurement.
  - Continue current combined oral contraceptive pill for now; clinician to reassess after examination (may change if migraines with aura are confirmed).
  - Clinician offered to prescribe a stronger analgesic (name/dose/frequency not documented); patient advised to take it with food.
  - Paracetamol may be taken in addition to the prescribed analgesic (as advised).
  - If headache resolves before the appointment, patient advised to cancel the appointment.
  - If headache becomes worse/unbearable or changes character, patient advised to go to A&E and/or contact for further advice.

- Follow-up and referrals:
  - Booked appointment with support team for physical exam and BP check; potential onward specialist referral dependent on findings.
  - No imaging or blood tests were ordered at time of transcript.

- Possible diagnosis: migraine (clinician’s impression).
- Need to reassess contraceptive suitability if migraine with aura is confirmed.
- Escalation plan: A&E if severe/worsening symptoms.
